# Visual Studio Code Documentation

> > Official documentation for Visual Studio Code, Microsoft's open-source AI-powered code editor with GitHub Copilot integration, supporting Python, Java, .NET, TypeScript, and remote development via WSL, containers, and SSH.

Visual Studio Code (VS Code) is a lightweight but powerful source code editor that runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux. It features built-in IntelliSense code completion, debugging, Git version control, and extensive extension support through the Visual Studio Marketplace.

## Key Topics

- Visual Studio Code (VS Code)
- GitHub Copilot
- IntelliSense
- Python development
- Java development
- .NET and C# Dev Kit
- Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL)
- Remote Development
- Dev Containers
- Git and version control
- TypeScript
- Debugging and testing
- Extensions and Marketplace
- AI-assisted coding
- Code navigation and editing

## Getting Started

- [Visual Studio Code - The open source AI code editor](https://code.visualstudio.com): Homepage: AI-powered code editor with GitHub Copilot integration
- [Download Visual Studio Code - Mac, Linux, Windows](https://code.visualstudio.com/download): Download VS Code for Mac, Linux, Windows; access Insiders build & vscode.dev
- [Documentation for Visual Studio Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs): Documentation hub: getting started, AI features, and GitHub Copilot guides
- [Tutorial: Get started with Visual Studio Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/getstarted/getting-started): Beginner tutorial: UI, IntelliSense, Code Actions, debugging & extensions
- [Getting started with Visual Studio Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/introvideos/basics): Getting started video tutorial: AI features, IntelliSense, and shortcuts
- [Introductory Videos](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/getstarted/introvideos): Video tutorial collection: overview of VS Code features for beginners
- [Visual Studio Code tips and tricks](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/getstarted/tips-and-tricks): Productivity tips: keyboard shortcuts, Command Palette, Emmet, IntelliSense
- [Why did we build Visual Studio Code?](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/editor/whyvscode): Product philosophy: lightweight editor with IntelliSense, debugging & Git support

## Setup and Installation

- [Setting up Visual Studio Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/setup/setup-overview): Setup overview: installation, platform support, updates, and Copilot Free plan
- [Visual Studio Code on Windows](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/setup/windows): Windows setup guide: install VS Code, WSL, Git, Node.js, and extensions
- [Visual Studio Code for the Web](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/setup/vscode-web): Browser-based VS Code at vscode.dev: zero-install GitHub & Azure Repos editing

## Language Support

- [Python in Visual Studio Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/languages/python): Python overview: Microsoft Python extension, IntelliSense, debugging, WSL support
- [Getting Started with Python in VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/python/python-tutorial): Python tutorial: setup Python 3, virtual environments, and debugging basics
- [Editing Python in Visual Studio Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/python/editing): Python editing: IntelliSense, autocomplete with Pylance & Pyright extensions
- [Java in Visual Studio Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/languages/java): Java overview: Extension Pack, Maven, Spring Boot, debugging with IntelliSense
- [Getting Started with Java in VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/java/java-tutorial): Java tutorial: setup JDK, Extension Pack for Java, Hello World guide
- [Using .NET in Visual Studio Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/languages/dotnet): .NET development setup: C# Dev Kit, F# extensions, and IntelliSense features

## Core Features

- [Basic editing](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/editing/codebasics): Basic editing features: keyboard shortcuts, multi-cursor, text selection
